title: app.bin (2MB compiled binary) committed to the repo
evidence: diff.patch: "diff --git a/app.bin b/app.bin" / "Binary files /dev/null and b/app.bin differ"; worktree: `git ls-files | grep app.bin` -> "app.bin"; `ls -la app.bin` -> "-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 moses staff 2057480 9 Aug 14:39 app.bin"
detail: A built macOS arm64 binary (2,057,480 bytes) is tracked at the repo root; .gitignore has no app.bin entry and nothing marks it deliberate. Build artifacts bloat the repo and are platform-specific.
recommended_fix: Remove app.bin from the tree (`git rm app.bin`), add `app.bin` to .gitignore, and commit; document the build command (tools/harness.sh pattern) in README.

title: Empty-ground click cannot dismiss an open router/pipe popover (dead deselect path)
evidence: press: "if nid, ok := prun.snap_node(&app.rc, f64(wx), f64(wy)); ok { app.press_node = nid; app.press_valid = true; app.drag.active = true; app.drag.from_node = nid }"; release: "if rl.IsMouseButtonReleased(.LEFT) && app.drag.active { ... if !moved { // a click, not a drag: select; handle_click_select(app, mouse, frame_ms) }"; handle_click_select tail: "app.sel = {} // empty ground closes the popover"
detail: drag.active is only set when the press snaps to a node, so a press on empty ground leaves the release branch unreachable and handle_click_select (the only path that clears sel) never runs. Canon #14 router select (inspect/triage popover) can only be closed via ESC or clicking another node/pipe — the natural mouse-only dismissal is inert.
recommended_fix: Handle release when !drag.active too: on an unmoved empty-ground click call handle_click_select (or clear app.sel) so clicking away closes the popover.

title: Grace countdown computes ticks × hz (inverted units) and discards the value
evidence:
secs := snap.grace_ticks_left * i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
		_ = secs
		txt := fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "!", 0)
detail: Converting ticks to seconds requires division by logic_hz; multiplying yields units of ticks²/s and the result is dead (`_ = secs`). The countdown pip draws regardless. If un-deadened, the readout would be wrong by hz² (100× at 10 Hz).
recommended_fix: Delete the dead secs computation, or compute secs := snap.grace_ticks_left / i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz) and render it.

title: App state fields press_valid and cosmetic_rng are written but never read
evidence: grep app/: press_valid declared "press_valid: bool," (line 29), written "app.press_valid = false" (197) and "app.press_valid = true" (203), zero reads; cosmetic_rng declared "cosmetic_rng: pp.Rng, // ODN-15 - cosmetics only, never the sim's" (39) and seeded "pp.rng_seed(&app.cosmetic_rng, fresh_seed() ~ 0xC05E)" (64), zero reads
detail: press_valid carries state the release handler never consults (release re-snaps instead), and the ODN-15 cosmetic RNG is seeded but no cosmetic system consumes it — both are inert fields suggesting unfinished intent.
recommended_fix: Remove press_valid, or use it in the release handler; wire cosmetic_rng to an actual cosmetic consumer (e.g. HUD jitter) or drop the field.

title: Snap generosity factor 1.6 hardcoded in snap.odin instead of catalog data
evidence:
radius_i := i64(f64(rc.catalogs.balance.snap_radius) * 1.6 + 0.5)
	r2 := radius_i * radius_i
--- data/balance.json: "  \"snap_radius\": 36,"
detail: E4 says snap is "inclusive at radius", and the catalog (ODN-5 single source) sets snap_radius=36 — but the effective radius is 58px (36×1.6, rounded). A gameplay-feel tuning literal lives in code, so balance.json stops being the single source for the snap boundary.
recommended_fix: Move the 1.6 generosity into balance.json (e.g. snap_radius_scale) or document it as a fixed UI constant; keep snap_radius the single tuning source.
